d: From a tree by the water to the fruit of the Spirit.
s: The righteous like a tree bringing fruit in its season.
God looked for fruit in his vineyard, Israel, and found oppression.
Jeremiah repeats the Psalm's tree by the water that never stops yielding fruit.
John the Baptist: trees without good fruit are cut down.
Jesus: good trees bring good fruit.
Jesus repeats John's warning nearly word for word.
Fruit comes from abiding in the vine.
Paul names the fruit: one fruit with nine qualities.

d: From the Spirit over the waters to the Spirit within.
s: The Spirit of God moved upon the waters.
David prays that God's holy spirit not be taken from him.
The spirit of the LORD will rest on the Branch.
God will put his spirit within his people.
God will pour out his spirit on all flesh.
Jesus: the Spirit of truth shall be in you.
The Spirit's fruit in everyday life.

d: A prayer for a clean heart becomes a promised covenant.
s: David prays: create in me a clean heart.
God will write his law in their hearts.
A heart of flesh for a heart of stone.
God repeats the promise: a new heart and a new spirit.
Blessed are the pure in heart.

d: Creation by speech, and the Word made flesh.
s: God speaks, and there is light.
By the word of the LORD were the heavens made.
A great light for people in darkness.
In the beginning was the Word.
Worlds framed by the word (rhēma) of God.
The Word of life, seen and handled.

d: From Moses to the fruit of the Spirit.
s: Moses, very meek above all men.
The meek shall inherit the earth.
Jesus: I am meek and lowly in heart.
Meekness as fruit of the Spirit.

d: Israel as God's vine, and Jesus as the true one.
s: Thou hast brought a vine out of Egypt.
The vineyard of the LORD is Israel; it yielded the wrong fruit.
The husbandman prunes for more fruit.
